sammendrag: Adults who do not complete secondary education often participate in basic skills programs to improve their literacy skills, acquire alternative secondary credentials, or transition into postsecondary education and higher paying jobs. Program evaluation data typically include only short-term outcomes and rarely include comparisons with matched nonparticipants. There is little rigorous research on the long-term impact of basic skills programs. This chapter considers findings from a longitudinal study of adults in the United States aged 18–44 who had not completed secondary education. A representative sample was interviewed and assessed six times over an 8-year period. The trajectories of the literacy skills and earnings of those who participated in adult basic skills programs are compared with those of carefully matched nonparticipants. Basic skills programs have a significant positive impact on long-term literacy development and earnings. These effects required, on average, 100 or more hours of attendance and took several years following program participation to fully mature.
tittel: Developmental Trajectories of Adult Education Students
